instruction: Locate the most recent email in the Notes folder and save its Word document attachment to the Desktop.

metadata.explanation: Task requires opening the latest email in Notes folder (subject: 'Lecture Document'), accessing the Word attachment 'lecture-notes.docx' (122101 bytes verified from cache), and saving it to the Desktop. Evaluator checks: (1) file exists at /home/user/Desktop/lecture-notes.docx (50%), (2) file is valid DOCX format via PK signature (30%), (3) file size >= 100KB indicating complete save (20%). This is a straightforward file save operation to Desktop, maintaining similar complexity to the original task.

llm_judge_reasons: Evaluator correctly verifies all requirements of the instruction: file saved to Desktop, valid DOCX format, and complete file transfer

Getter logic is sound: extracts file from correct path (/home/user/Desktop/lecture-notes.docx), checks existence, validates DOCX format via PK signature (DOCX files are ZIP archives), and verifies file size
Metric comparison logic is correct: checks existence (50%), format validation (30%), and size threshold >= 100KB (20%) with appropriate scoring breakdown
Expected value (min_size: 100000) is semantically correct - the actual file is 122101 bytes per metadata, so 100KB threshold appropriately verifies complete save
Data flow is correct: getter extracts file state -> metric compares existence/format/size -> returns appropriate score
No edge case issues: handles missing files gracefully (returns exists=False), validates format before size check
No parameter handling issues: metric correctly accesses expected.get('min_size', 100000) for rule-type expected values
